*2027 intake*

# Study MBBS in the Philippines

A complete guide for Indian students planning MBBS in the Philippines, from choosing the right college to landing in Cebu, Manila or Davao. Eligible colleges, the acceptance letter, the BSBio course, visa documents, flight booking, departure and arrival, college enrolment, and what the five and a half years actually cost.

[Compare the six colleges](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md)
[What you need before you go](https://drdreams.in/index.md#before-you-go)

Every page carries the date it was last checked. How to correct a page is on [the about page](https://drdreams.in/about/index.md).

## The basics

Degree
:   Doctor of Medicine (MD)

Duration
:   5.5 to 6 years, internship included

Language
:   English throughout

Typical total, all in
:   Rs 28 to 35 lakh

College fees alone
:   Rs 20 to 24 lakh

Recognition
:   NMC list and WDOMS, check both

Colleges covered here
:   6 in Cebu, Manila, Davao

**November 2026: the Philippine licence is now open.**

Indian graduates of recognised Philippine medical schools can now sit the Physician Licensure Examination and register to practise in the Philippines, after the Philippine Professional Regulation Commission cleared the reciprocity rule. The Embassy of India, Manila confirmed it. It does not replace FMGE or NExT for practising in India. [What changed, and what it does not](https://drdreams.in/ple-philippines/index.md).

*Start here*

## What you need before you go

Five things, in the order they matter. Get these right and the rest is paperwork.

1. ### Which are the NMC approved medical colleges in the Philippines?

   Start with the [NMC list of recognised foreign medical institutions](https://www.nmc.org.in), then look up the same college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). A college missing from either list is a problem you cannot fix after five years. All six colleges here are on both, and the [college page](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md) links each one to the register. Check them yourself anyway.
2. ### What is the BSBio course, and do you need it?

   BSBio is the pre-medical year before the MD, and Indian students without a bachelor's degree take it. It runs one academic year at most colleges and has to be CHED recognised. Not every place runs it the same way: Kings Academy in India offers its own BSBio, six months to a year, and the duration varies from college to college, so ask the college you are joining whether it will accept the shorter one you are being offered. BSBio does not replace NEET. NMC still expects NEET cleared before the MD starts. [How the BSBio route works](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md#without-neet).
3. ### How many years is MBBS in the Philippines?

   5.5 to 6 years is standard. The MD is four years, the fourth is a full clinical clerkship, then a twelve-month internship. Add the BSBio year if you need it. NMC's Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate Regulations, notified on 18 November 2021, ask for 54 months of study excluding the internship, and CHED's letter to the Indian Embassy says the Philippine MD meets its conditions. Ask the college for the curriculum with the month count, and for the line that says where the internship sits. [The 54-month rule and the notice behind it](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules/index.md#fmgl-2021).
4. ### How much does MBBS in the Philippines cost?

   Rs 28 lakh to Rs 35 lakh on average, with college fees at Rs 20 lakh to Rs 24 lakh of that. The rest is hostel, food, flights, visa renewals, insurance and a buffer. The published hostel and food package runs 14,000 to 15,000 pesos a month, about Rs 20,000; sharing a room and cooking brings it down to 8,000 to 10,000 pesos. DMSF runs higher, around Rs 38 lakh, because its tuition is quoted in dollars. [The lines, one by one](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost/index.md).
5. ### What is the best part of the Philippines?

   The people, the lifestyle, the weather, the language, and a bit of Indian ancestry you will notice in the food and the names. Classes and hospital work are in English. [Life in the Philippines](https://drdreams.in/student-life/index.md), and [life outside studies](https://drdreams.in/life-outside-studies/index.md).

*Colleges*

## Six colleges, and why only six

Out of the hundreds of medical colleges in the Philippines, these are six that I and my team have experienced by studying at or visiting them. All six are following the latest NMC/MCI rules, have administrations that are used to Indian students, and are listed in NMC and WDOMS.

Only these six are here, for one reason: curriculum compliance with the latest NMC gazette rule and the embassy clarification, which asks for 54 months of medical studies and a twelve-month internship. The rules are still being drafted at college level, so ask each college for the current position in writing. [The gazette date, the 2026 notice and the official PDF](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules/index.md).

*The doubts*

## Doubts students and parents ask about

These come up every time, in the words people actually type, so they are answered here and on the linked page.

**Is MBBS in the Philippines valid in India?**

Yes, completely valid, as long as the college was on the NMC list when you joined and when you graduated, and you clear FMGE, or NExT when it comes. More than 15,000 students have graduated from the Philippines and cleared FMGE in India, counting every pass from 2002 to now across the whole country. The [NBEMS site](https://natboard.edu.in) publishes the results session by session, so you can add it up yourself.

The only catch is the exam. In 2025, 884 of 4,655 Philippine-trained candidates passed in June and 903 of 4,864 passed in December, about 19 per cent each session, according to the [NBEMS FMGE performance report](https://natboard.edu.in). Start preparing in first year, not after the internship. [What the rules require](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules/index.md#validity).

**Is the Philippines safe for Indian students?**

Yes. Try comparing the official crime rate of India and the Philippines yourself. [Numbeo's 2026 mid-year table](https://www.numbeo.com/crime/rankings_by_country.jsp) puts India's crime index at 44.2 and the Philippines at 43.4, and the safety index at 55.8 and 56.6. On a 0 to 100 scale, where a lower crime index is safer, the two countries are level.

| Country | Crime index | Safety index |
| --- | --- | --- |
| India | 44.2 | 55.8 |
| Philippines | 43.4 | 56.6 |

*Numbeo, 2026 mid-year, 0 to 100. Lower crime index is safer. The HTML page shows the same numbers as a bar chart. [WorldData.info](https://www.worlddata.info/criminality.php) says the same: India 57.7, the Philippines 56.2.*

I lived in Cebu for five and a half years and never felt unsafe walking home. That is one person in one city, so the table is the part that matters. If someone tells you the Philippines is dangerous and India is not, they are not looking at the same table.

**Can I study MBBS in the Philippines without NEET?**

You can start, but you cannot finish and practise in India without it. Some colleges admit students to the BSBio year without NEET, and the student clears NEET before moving into the MD. NMC wants NEET for an Indian student who plans to practise in India, with no exceptions. The BSBio year buys time to prepare. It does not replace the exam. [How the BSBio route works](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md#without-neet).

**How much does MBBS in the Philippines cost?**

Rs 28 lakh to Rs 35 lakh for the whole stay, with college fees at Rs 20 lakh to Rs 24 lakh of that. The rest is hostel, food, flights, visa renewals, insurance and a buffer. The published hostel and food package runs 14,000 to 15,000 pesos a month, about Rs 20,000; sharing a room and cooking brings it down to 8,000 to 10,000 pesos. DMSF runs higher, around Rs 38 lakh, because its tuition is quoted in dollars. [The lines, one by one](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost/index.md).

**Is the Philippines better than Russia, Georgia or India?**

For an Indian student, the language is the difference. Russia, China, Georgia and Ukraine teach in their own script, so you learn a language before you learn medicine. The Philippines teaches in English and writes in English letters, which is the most advantageous part. Against India, the whole programme lands below many private Indian seats, and it is a five to six hour flight home. Against Russia and Georgia, it costs around what Georgia quotes. [The country comparison, line by line](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines-vs-other-countries/index.md).

**Do Indian students need to learn Tagalog or Cebuano?**

Not necessarily. Lectures, hospital notes and paperwork are in English, and you can finish the degree without a word of either. But if you want to be treated as one of the locals, learning some helps, and it is easier than the other destinations: both languages are written in English letters, so there is no new script like Russia, China, Georgia or Ukraine. [Language and daily life](https://drdreams.in/student-life/index.md).

**Will I find Indian food easily?**

Yes. Everyone loves Indian food, Filipinos included, and in every locality you will find at least one Indian restaurant, north Indian and south Indian, with different menus. The warning is that it is slightly expensive, and nothing beats food cooked in its own country. If you want to eat local, try adobo, chicken or pork, or their chicken curry, close to ours with less masala. [Food, weekends and festivals](https://drdreams.in/life-outside-studies/index.md).

**What can I do after the 5.5 years of MD?**

Two paths. In India, clear FMGE, then register with a state medical council. Some states, Karnataka and Andhra among them, have allowed registration after five and a half years; others want the twelve-month CRMI first. It depends on the state board, so confirm with the council where you plan to work. There are draft rules that would let a PLE-licensed graduate skip the CRMI and register on an FMGE score of 150 or above, but they are drafts, not notified rules. In the Philippines, clear the PLE and register, then specialise or work as a GP. Speaking Filipino by then is an advantage, because people are welcoming. [FMGE, NExT and the timeline after the degree](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next/index.md#after).

*Documents*

## Documents, from acceptance letter to enrolment

Three lists, and the third one is the one people leave until the last week.

### For admission and the acceptance letter

Class 10 and 12 marksheets, NEET scorecard and admit card, passport with at least eighteen months of validity, birth certificate, photographs, and a police clearance through the Passport Seva Portal. Each item has a format and an authentication step. [The full checklist](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md#documents).

### For the 9(F) student visa

The acceptance letter, attested documents, a financial affidavit, a medical certificate from a NABH-accredited hospital, and a six-month bank statement with a closing balance of Rs 3,00,000. The college issues a support letter. [The visa file, step by step](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md).

### Before you come home

Degree certificate, full transcript, internship completion certificate, English medium certificate, and the apostille and Indian embassy authentication on the documents you will submit in India. Keep the passport with every visa stamp, and keep scans in two places. [The list to keep for the rest of your career](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules/index.md#keep).

### If you are going somewhere other than India

The same papers go to different bodies: [ECFMG](https://www.ecfmg.org) for the USMLE, [AMC](https://www.amc.org.au) for Australia, the [GMC](https://www.gmc-uk.org) for the PLAB, and the [DHA](https://www.dha.gov.ae) for Dubai. Each wants the degree and transcript verified by the university, usually apostilled. Start before your last semester ends.

*Five years*

## My life in the Philippines, year by year

I did the MD at Southwestern in Cebu and finished in 2025. Short version, with the shops, rides and offices you end up knowing.

### First year: BSBio

Anatomy, physiology and biochemistry, at a pace that surprises everyone who prepared for NEET. Classes are in English and the accent takes about a month. Most of the year goes into finding things: the printing shop for handouts, the Goto stall near the gate, and which jeepney from campus reaches the mall without a transfer.

### Second year: the proper medical subjects start

This is where the batch splits into people who study together and people who study alone. Both pass. The ones who finish with a good FMGE score and a social life are usually in the first group. Start the FMGE syllabus now, an hour a week, instead of saving it for the internship year. Groceries come from SM or Ayala, parcels from Shopee and Lazada with a week or two of patience, and documents move across town by Lalamove when you cannot leave the lab.

### Third year: pathology, pharmacology, and the hospital

Theory ends and the hospital starts. You buy the white coat and the rubber shoes that survive a twelve-hour duty, and you learn that the ward is a different kind of tired from the library. Cebu's hospitals are busy and students are expected to work, not watch.

### Fourth year: the clinical clerkship

A full twelve-month rotating clerkship, so it is the year of duty schedules, endorsements and sleep in the hospital canteen. Medicine, surgery, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, and the community. Grab at five in the morning becomes a normal expense. Your Cebuano improves faster here than in three years of classes, because patients do not slow down for you.

### Fifth year: internship, and the flight home

The internship feels like a job with a student badge. Notes, case presentations, questions at seven in the morning. The paperwork for home starts here too: transcript, internship certificate, apostille at the Department of Foreign Affairs, authentication at the Embassy of India in Manila. Book the flight after the documents are in hand, and book it as a return.

### Getting around

Jeepneys cover most student routes and cost coins. Habal-habal is the motorcycle taxi that gets you up a hill a jeepney will not. Angkas and Maxim are the bike apps you book. Grab is the car app, and it took over Uber's operations in 2018, so it is what people mean when they say Uber here. Lalamove moves documents and furniture, Shopee and Lazada deliver everything else, slowly. Buses run between cities and to the airports at Mactan, Manila and Davao.

### Markets and shops

Carbon Market in Cebu and Bankerohan in Davao are where the cheap vegetables and fish are. In Manila it is Divisoria and Quiapo. Malls, SM and Ayala, cover everything else, and the smaller supermarkets near campus are open later than the big ones.

### Offices you will visit

The Bureau of Immigration handles visa conversion in your first weeks and the extensions after that, with offices in Manila, Cebu and Davao. The Embassy of India in Manila handles passport work and document authentication. The Professional Regulation Commission handles the PLE. All three keep weekday hours, close for lunch, and publish holidays at short notice, so check the official page on the morning you go.

- [Bureau of Immigration](https://immigration.gov.ph)
- [Bureau of Immigration, Cebu, on the map](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Bureau+of+Immigration+Cebu)
- [Bureau of Immigration, Davao, on the map](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Bureau+of+Immigration+Davao)
- [Embassy of India, Manila](https://www.eoimanila.gov.in)
- [Embassy of India, Manila, on the map](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Embassy+of+India+Manila)
- [Professional Regulation Commission](https://www.prc.gov.ph)

### Weather, working hours and rush hour

Two seasons and neither is cold. December to May is dry and hot, around 32°C most days. June to November is wet, and July to October brings the typhoons that occasionally suspend classes. Offices open at eight and close at five on weekdays, malls run from ten to nine, and banks close mid-afternoon. Rush hour is seven to nine in the morning and five to eight in the evening. If your duty starts at seven, leave before six.

![Boats on clear turquoise water at a beach in Cebu, Philippines](https://drdreams.in/about/gallery-cebu-beach-boats.jpg)

*Cebu. Five and a half years of it. The beach is not the reason to go, but it is not nothing.*

*The mechanics*

## Overview and timeline of getting admission

Five steps, in order. The full version, with the document list and the visa paperwork, is on the process page.

1. ### Research the college, then choose agency or direct

   The first-year fee is the part that differs between agencies, because year one is BSBio, not medicine. From year two you pay the college directly, at the college's own rate, so that number stays the same whoever sends you. Ask two or three agencies and the college itself, and get the whole course in one written quotation, broken into BSBio, document attestation in Delhi, police clearance, visa, insurance, tickets, books and uniform. Pay in instalments, never the full amount, and read the refund rule before the first one. Agencies will tell you that no college in the Philippines accepts direct admission except Southwestern. Ask the college's international office yourself, because several of the six answer email. [What the money is buying](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost/index.md).
2. ### Apply through the agency, or email the college

   For direct admission, email the college's official address with the documents and ask for the acceptance letter. If you are going through an agency, the acceptance letter and the attestation are their job, and you should still receive copies of everything. [The document list](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md#documents).
3. ### Apply for the 9(F) student visa

   The acceptance letter plus the attested documents, the medical test and the financial papers. Doing this yourself is possible and time consuming. A visa consultant earns the fee here, because one rejection costs a semester. [The visa file, step by step](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md).
4. ### Attend the visa interview

   Chennai for the southern states, and Mumbai, Kolkata or Delhi. You will be given a tentative date for the visa, so do not book anything until it arrives in writing.
5. ### Book the flight, land, enrol

   Book the actual ticket after the visa is in hand, and book it as a return. Agencies sometimes book a dummy return to satisfy the airline while the real return is still open; make sure you know which one you are holding before you fly. Arrange a pickup before you land, or have the agency confirm theirs. Then enrolment and orientation, and the [student life page](https://drdreams.in/student-life/index.md) covers the month after that.

*The honest version*

## What the degree gives you, and what it does not

An MD from a listed Philippine college is recognised in India. That is the whole promise, and it holds only while the college stays on the list. It does not make you a doctor in India on graduation day.

You still sit FMGE or NExT, and you still complete a year of internship in India before you can register. Students who treat that as a formality end up repeating the exam. Students who start in first year clear it.

The clinical training is genuinely good. Philippine hospitals are busy, and foreign students are allowed hands on patients, which is not true everywhere. That is the part worth paying for.

*The whole route*

# MBBS in the Philippines: complete guide for Indian students

One page that runs from the degree to the licence: what the MD is, what it costs, how recognition works, how to get in, and what happens after you graduate.

*Reviewed 25 November 2026. Written by Dr. Nitz, a 2025 graduate of Southwestern University, Cebu.*

## On this page

1. [Why students choose it](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#why)
2. [The degree, and how long it takes](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#degree)
3. [Recognition in India](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#recognition)
4. [The six colleges](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#colleges)
5. [What it costs](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#cost)
6. [NEET and the BSBio year](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#neet)
7. [Getting in](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#admission)
8. [What the week looks like](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#life)
9. [The four expensive mistakes](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#mistakes)
10. [A timeline for the 2027 intake](https://drdreams.in/mbbs-in-philippines/index.md#timeline)

## 1. Why students choose it

There are four honest reasons, and one bad one.

The first is language. Lectures, textbooks, hospital charts and patients are all in English. In Russia or China you spend the first years learning a language just to understand a ward round. Here you start as a medical student on day one.

The second is clinical access. Philippine hospitals are busy, and students are allowed to examine patients, assist in deliveries and stand in theatre from the clinical years. In several other destinations foreign students watch. Watching is not the same as doing, and the difference shows up when you sit an exam that tests clinical judgement.

The third is the shape of the degree. It follows the American model: a four-year MD after a bachelor's, with the internship built into the programme. You graduate with a Doctor of Medicine, which NMC treats as equivalent to MBBS for Indian registration.

The fourth is distance and culture. Flights from India run five to six hours, the climate is tropical, and Filipino families are warm to Indian students in a way that makes the first year survivable. Cebu in particular feels less like a foreign country than like a very different Indian city.

The bad reason is that it looks cheap in a brochure. It is cheaper than a private Indian medical seat. It is not cheap, and it is not a shortcut. Treat it as a long, expensive, serious course of study that happens to be abroad.

## 2. The degree, and how long it takes

You graduate with a **Doctor of Medicine (MD)**. In the Philippines that is the primary medical degree, not a postgraduate one. NMC recognises it as equivalent to MBBS for the purpose of Indian registration, provided the college is on the list.

The programme runs about **five and a half years including internship**. The first two years are classroom and laboratory: anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, then pathology, pharmacology, microbiology and the rest. Third year onwards you are in the hospital. The final year is a rotating internship.

If you take the BSBio pre-medical year first, add six months to a year. That route exists mainly for students who still need to clear NEET, and [it has its own section](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md#without-neet).

One warning about duration. Curricula change, and NMC's requirements have tightened. A college that quotes you four years is either describing an old programme or a compressed one that will cause you problems at registration. Ask for the current curriculum in writing.

## 3. Recognition in India

This is the section to read twice.

Your degree is useful in India if, and only if, the college appears on the National Medical Commission's list of recognised foreign medical institutions. Not "will be listed soon". Not "in process". On the list, when you enrol, and when you graduate.

Check two places before you pay anything:

- The NMC's own list, at [nmc.org.in](https://www.nmc.org.in).
- The World Directory of Medical Schools, at [search.wdoms.org](https://search.wdoms.org). NMC's 2026 notice leans on this directory for verification.

Then there is the part nobody puts in the brochure. After the MD, you sit **FMGE**, which is being replaced by **NExT** over time, and you complete a **twelve month internship in India** before you register with a state medical council. The exam is hard, and the students who fail are usually the ones who planned to start preparing after graduation. [More on both exams](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next/index.md).

The 2026 rules added detail on the 54 month requirement, compensation for any online teaching, and internship verification. [The full notice, with the official PDF](https://drdreams.in/mci-rules/index.md), is worth an hour of your time before you commit.

## 4. The six colleges

Six are covered here: one studied at, three visited, and all six known through graduates worth trusting. Three sit in Cebu, one in Metro Manila, two in Davao. They differ in cost, in batch size, in hospital size, and in whether FMGE coaching happens on campus.

The six colleges, in the order we would shortlist them for a typical budget.

| College | City | Best for | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**GCM Gullas**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md#gcm-gullas) | Cebu | Lowest entry cost, on-campus FMGE coaching | Large batch, basic hostel |
| [**Southwestern**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md#southwestern) | Cebu | Hospital rotations, smaller Indian batch | No in-house FMGE coaching |
| [**Perpetual Help**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md#perpetual) | Las Piñas | Indian community, food, coaching | Manila traffic, higher living cost |
| [**DMSF**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md#dmsf) | Davao | Clinical volume, anatomy lab | Higher fees, longer flight home |
| [**Brokenshire**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md#brokenshire) | Davao | Small batches, faculty attention | Smaller attached hospital |
| [**Jose Maria**](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md#jmc) | Davao | Tightest budget, medical missions | Cook for yourself, basic facilities |

[The comparison page](https://drdreams.in/colleges/index.md) has fees, food, batch size and the rating side by side.

## 5. What it costs

For the whole programme, tuition plus hostel plus food plus flights plus visa renewals, most families land between **Rs 28 lakh and Rs 35 lakh**. The spread comes from the college, the city, and whether you cook or eat out.

A private Indian medical seat, by comparison, is quoted in tens of lakhs for tuition alone, before donation. That gap is why this option exists at all. It is not a small amount of money, and a quote that presents it as cheap is worth checking line by line.

The [cost page](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost/index.md) breaks the total into each component and compares it with Russia, Georgia, China and Kazakhstan.

## 6. NEET and the BSBio year

NMC requires NEET for Indian students who intend to practise in India. That is the rule, and nothing waives it.

What exists is a workaround in timing, not in requirement. You enrol in BSBio, a pre-medical biology year at a Philippine university, without NEET. While you study, you prepare for and sit NEET. Once you clear it, you move into the MD at the same university. You lose six months to a year, and you gain a year of English-medium science teaching and a soft landing in a new country.

Students who have already done a year of serious NEET coaching usually skip BSBio and go straight to the MD, provided their NEET score qualifies them. [The process page has the detail](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md#without-neet), including what BSBio does and does not fix.

## 7. Getting in

The short version: pick the college, email its international office, send documents, get the acceptance letter, apply for the visa, fly. There is no entrance exam of the kind you are imagining, and there is no lottery.

The documents are ones you already have or can obtain in a week: 10th and 12th marksheets, passport, birth certificate, police clearance, medical fitness certificate, photographs. The [process page](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md) lists them with the order of operations and the visa steps.

The process is mostly email and patience. The one stage where paying someone is reasonable is the visa file, if your documents are messy or you have a refusal on record, because a rejected application costs a semester.

## 8. What the week looks like

Classes in the morning, lab or ward in the afternoon, and then the real work: figuring out dinner. Food is the thing every Indian student underestimates. Cebu has Indian restaurants and spice shops, but not on every corner. Learn to cook three things before you leave.

The accent takes about a month to tune into. The heat takes about a week. The loneliness takes longer, and it is the reason to pick a college with a decent Indian batch if you are the kind of person who needs company. [Food, safety, housing and money, in detail](https://drdreams.in/student-life/index.md).

## 9. The four expensive mistakes

- **Paying a deposit before checking the college.** Check the NMC list first. It takes two minutes and it is free.
- **Choosing on first-year fees alone.** A cheap first year with expensive later years is a sales technique, not a discount.
- **Starting FMGE preparation in the final year.** By then the subjects you need are two years behind you. Start in first year, slowly.
- **Believing the college will handle your registration.** The college handles its paperwork. Yours is yours, and NMC's verification is strict about the internship and the 54 month requirement.

[The document checklist](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md#documents), and how to check a fee quote.

## 10. A timeline for the 2027 intake

Months move between colleges, so treat this as a shape rather than a schedule, and confirm dates with the admissions office.

1. **Now to February.** Shortlist two or three colleges. Check each on the NMC and WDOMS lists. Get the current fee sheet from each in writing.
2. **February to April.** Prepare documents. Sit NEET if you have not. Speak to students in your shortlisted colleges before you choose.
3. **April to June.** Apply. Receive the acceptance letter. Start the visa file.
4. **June to August.** Visa, flight, hostel reservation, first month of money in a Philippine bank account once you land.
5. **August onwards.** Enrolment and the first semester. Join or form a study group early, because the FMGE clock starts now, not in year four.

**The one line version.**

Pick a college that is on the NMC list, confirm the total cost in writing, learn to cook, and start FMGE preparation in first year. Everything else is detail, and the detail is on the pages linked above.

*Questions*

## What families ask before they commit

**How long does MBBS take in the Philippines?**

About five and a half years including internship. Add six months to a year if you take the BSBio pre-medical route. Confirm the current curriculum with the college in writing, because it has changed before.

**Is NEET required to study medicine in the Philippines?**

NMC requires NEET for Indian students who intend to practise in India. Some colleges admit students to BSBio without it, and the student clears NEET before the MD. Going without NEET and expecting to practise in India is the mistake, not the BSBio year.

**Is the Philippines better than Russia or China?**

The teaching is in English, patients speak English, and foreign students get hands on clinical work, which is not true in every destination. The trade off is cost and distance from home. Whether it is better depends on your budget and how you handle being far away, not on a ranking.

**What happens after the MD?**

You sit FMGE or NExT, complete a twelve month internship in India, then register with the state medical council. Plan for that exam from the first year, not the last. [Both exams explained](https://drdreams.in/fmge-next/index.md).

## The next page to read

*Cost is the part families underestimate, and the part most quotes are vague about. The numbers, line by line, are on the next page.*

[See what it costs](https://drdreams.in/fees-and-cost/index.md)
[The admission process](https://drdreams.in/admission-process/index.md)

*Cebu City*

## GCM Gullas College of Medicine (UV Gullas)

The lowest entry cost of the six, with on-campus FMGE coaching, an in-house Indian mess, and heavy clinical exposure at Vicente Sotto Memorial Medical Center. It has the largest Indian batch in Cebu and functional, basic hostels. When total budget is the deciding factor, this is the standard baseline choice.

*★★★★★ Reviewed November 2026. Verified from official UV Gullas documentation, CHED/NMC compliance filings, and current student reports.*

## About the College

Established in 1977 as the medical school of the University of the Visayas (founded in 1919 by Don Vicente Gullas), the UV Gullas College of Medicine operates from its dedicated medical campus in Banilad. The institution is recognized by the World Health Organization (WDOMS) and the National Medical Commission (NMC). Its curriculum adheres to the US-patterned medical model with English-medium instruction throughout.

> **Official Motto:** *"Amor, Servitium, Humanitas"* (Love, Leadership, and Service to Humanity)  
> **Official Vision:** *"To serve the world and serve humanity through excellence in healthcare and affordable medical education."*  
> **College Mission:** *"To prepare young minds with excellence in medical education, techniques, and core values such as honesty, accountability, and inquisitiveness."*

## The facts

Location & Address
:   6014 Gov. M. Cuenco Avenue, Banilad, Mandaue City / Cebu City, 6014 Cebu, Philippines

Programme Structure
:   BS Biology (Pre-Med) + 4-Year Doctor of Medicine (MD) + 12-Month Clinical Internship (Total 5.5–6 Years; NMC 54+12 Month Compliant)

Instruction Language
:   English (100% of lectures, practicals, exams, and ward rounds)

FMGE / NExT Coaching
:   Yes, integrated on-campus coaching by visiting Indian medical faculty and KINGS medical coaching

Official Website
:   [uvgullasmedicalcollege.com](https://uvgullasmedicalcollege.com) / [uvgullas.com](https://uvgullas.com)

**The short version.**

Best value for money among Philippine medical universities. Cebu is manageable, the hospital rotation bed volume is substantial, and the campus includes structured FMGE coaching. Expect a large Indian peer group, basic dormitories, and high competition for faculty attention in practical sessions.

**Information sourcing.**

Compiled from official University of the Visayas medical bulletins, 2026–2027 fee circulars, and verified reports from active student council representatives and recent graduates.

## International Student Facilities

- **International Students Help Desk:** An on-campus support office handles 9(F) student visa endorsement, biometric Bureau of Immigration clearances, NBI police clearances, ACR I-Card renewals, and local barangay certificates.
- **Hostel Accommodation:** Separate campus-affiliated hostels for male and female students with 24/7 biometric access, security guard posts, CCTV monitoring, study tables, and optional air-conditioned rooms.
- **In-House Indian Mess:** Full-time canteen managed by Indian cooks providing daily North Indian and South Indian vegetarian and non-vegetarian meal plans.
- **Affiliated Teaching Hospitals:** Clinical rotations operate through Vicente Sotto Memorial Medical Center (VSMMC - 1,200+ bed government apex hospital), Chong Hua Hospital, Perpetual Succour Hospital, and Gullas Memorial Hospital.
- **Advanced Facilities:** 3D Anatomage digital dissection tables, bone laboratories, simulation manikins, and an air-conditioned medical library.
- **Scholarships & Merit Concessions:** Academic merit fee reductions are granted to top academic scorers in pre-med coursework and annual MD semester rankings, awarded directly by the Dean's Office.

*The good*

## What works here

- **The entry cost is the lowest of the six.** For a family that has a hard ceiling, this is the college that keeps the whole five years inside it.
- **FMGE coaching is on campus.** That sounds small until year four, when the alternative is an online course, a lot of self-discipline and nobody checking whether you watched it.
- **Cebu is the easier city.** Smaller than Manila, cheaper, and calmer. Students move around at night here in a way they do not in parts of Metro Manila.
- **Hospital exposure is real.** The affiliated hospitals are busy, and students get into the wards rather than watching from a corridor.
- **Food is manageable.** Limited compared with Manila, but Cebu has Indian restaurants and spice shops, and the college area has places that will cook for you.
- **Large Indian batch.** If you are the kind of student who needs company to survive the first year, this is a feature, not a flaw.

*The trade*

## What you give up

- **The batch is large.** You will not be a name to most faculty in the first two years. If you learn by being noticed and questioned, that is a real cost.
- **The hostel is basic.** Clean enough, not comfortable. Do not arrive expecting air conditioning and privacy at the lowest price quoted.
- **Competition for attention.** A big batch means fewer minutes per student in practicals. The students who do well here are the ones who ask first.
- **It is a value pick, not a prestige pick.** Nobody in India will be impressed by the name. What matters is the NMC listing and your FMGE score.

*Fit*

## Who should pick it

A student with a clear budget ceiling who does not need to be the only Indian in the room, and who will use the on-campus coaching instead of treating it as optional. It also suits families who want the city to be the safe, boring part of the decision.

*Not for*

## Who should skip it

Anyone who needs small classes and personal attention, anyone who cannot handle a crowd, and anyone whose plan depends on a comfortable hostel. Look at [Brokenshire](#brokenshire) for attention or [Perpetual](#perpetual) for a bigger Indian community.

*Money*

## Fees for the 2026-2027 intake

Published by the college for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges (enrolment, Level 1 semesters, documentation, visa, ticketing, books) are already quoted in rupees.

Fee sheet, GCM Gullas College of Medicine, 2026-2027

| Particular | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Enrolment and admission fee | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 1st semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing and other services | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Book fee | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | 1,25,000 PHP (Rs 1,80,966) |
| Food and accommodation per month | 14,000 PHP (Rs 20,268) |

- FMGE coaching: face-to-face coaching by Indian doctors, on the Gullas and KINGS campus.
- Visa costs in the Philippines: visa conversion and extension are paid by the student at actual cost.
- Refund: the enrolment fee is not refunded.

**Campus facilities:** 3D Anatomage, laboratory, classroom, auditorium, hospital, library.

**What the admissions package includes:** MEA and foreign-affairs authentication, apostille of academic documents, visa appointment and preparation, embassy visa interview fee, visa from the Philippines embassy in India, foreign-exchange assistance, one India-Philippines flight ticket, airport pickup and transfer to the hostel, and a Philippines mobile SIM.

*Fees change every intake. Confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay, and use the ask list below for the lines the sheet does not cover.*

*Money*

## What to ask the college for

The sheet above is the 2026-2027 figure published by the college. Fees change every intake, so confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay. Ask the admissions office for these things as well:

1. ### The current fee sheet, with the year printed on it

   Tuition per year, not per semester, and the total for the full programme.
2. ### What the hostel costs, separately

   Per month or per semester, and what is included. Ask whether air conditioning is extra.
3. ### Which fees are refundable

   If your visa is refused, what comes back and what does not.
4. ### Whether FMGE coaching is included

   On campus, and whether it is part of tuition or a separate charge later.
5. ### The internship arrangement

   Which hospital, for how long, and whether it satisfies NMC's onsite requirement.
6. ### The written confirmation of your seat

   On college letterhead, before you transfer money to anyone.

Then compare the totals on the [cost page](/fees-and-cost/), including flights and visa renewals. The cheapest first year is not always the cheapest degree.

## Before you pay anyone

**Verify, in this order.**

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet, from the college's own admissions office, not from the person asking you to pay.

If a broker cannot tell you where the college appears on those two lists, that is your answer.

Official website: [uvgullasmedicalcollege.com](https://uvgullasmedicalcollege.com) / [uvgullas.com](https://uvgullas.com). For direct fee breakdowns and unbiased guidance, contact Dr. Nitz.

[The document checklist](/admission-process/#documents) is worth ten minutes before any payment.

*Cebu City*

## Southwestern University PHINMA (SWU School of Medicine)

Established medical university in Cebu City with deep clinical rotation volume at Sacred Heart Hospital (SWU Medical Center) and Vicente Sotto Memorial Medical Center. Features a smaller, more integrated Indian batch and English immersion, requiring self-directed FMGE preparation.

*★★★★☆ Reviewed November 2026. Verified from official SWU PHINMA academic circulars, CHED/NMC listings, and active student reports.*

## About the College

Founded in 1946 in Cebu City and acquired by the PHINMA Education network in 2015, Southwestern University School of Medicine is one of the pioneer medical institutions in the Visayas and Mindanao. Recognized by WHO (WDOMS) and the National Medical Commission (NMC), SWU operates an integrated spiral medical curriculum emphasizing early patient contact and clinical problem-solving.

> **Official Motto:** *"Scientia, Integritas, Fidelitas"* (Science, Integrity, Fidelity)  
> **Institutional Vision:** *"To provide an inclusive, innovative, and diverse learning environment, extending quality healthcare education through modern clinical practice."*  
> **Mission Attribute:** *"Developing competent, compassionate, communicative, and leadership-oriented healthcare practitioners."*

## The facts

Location & Address
:   Urgello Street, Sambag II, Cebu City, 6000 Cebu, Philippines

Programme Structure
:   BS Biology + 4-Year Doctor of Medicine (MD) + 12-Month Clinical Internship (Total 5.5–6 Years; NMC 54+12 Month Compliant)

Instruction Language
:   English (100% of lectures, practicals, exams, and clinical duties)

FMGE / NExT Coaching
:   Self-directed (no compulsory on-campus faculty coaching; students subscribe to online Indian preparation platforms)

Official Website
:   [swu.edu.ph](https://swu.edu.ph)

**The short version.**

High-yield clinical rotations with hands-on ward responsibilities. The smaller Indian batch forces faster English fluency and local adaptation. Students must be disciplined self-starters who arrange their own FMGE study schedule from year one.

**Information sourcing.**

Compiled from official SWU PHINMA registrar bulletins, hospital affiliation records, and verified feedback from recent clinical clerks and graduates.

## International Student Facilities

- **International Students Help Desk:** Dedicated foreign student liaison handling 9(F) student visa endorsement, ACR I-Card processing, and quarantine clearances. Notably accepts direct international admissions.
- **Hostel Accommodation:** On-campus dormitories and verified private apartments within walking distance along Urgello and Aznar Coliseum with 24/7 security.
- **Food & Living:** No dedicated institutional Indian mess; students cook for themselves using induction cooktops or eat at nearby Cebu canteens and Indian restaurants.
- **Clinical Hospitals:** Southwestern University Medical Center (Sacred Heart Hospital - 200+ bed university tertiary hospital), Vicente Sotto Memorial Medical Center (VSMMC - 1,200+ bed apex government center), and Cebu City Medical Center.
- **Scholarships & Merit Concessions:** PHINMA academic excellence tuition discounts and Dean's Honors List concessions awarded based on semester GPA.

*The good*

## What works here

- **The clinical years are the real thing.** Busy wards, real patients, and students are expected to work rather than observe. Students deliver babies and assist in theatre here.
- **Faculty who have practised.** The clinicians teaching you have seen the cases they describe. That sounds obvious. It is not universal.
- **Small Indian batch.** Fewer countrymen means more English spoken, more Filipino friends, and less time in a comfort bubble. That is the difference between passing and coasting.
- **An established university.** The campus has been running long enough that the processes, however slow, exist and work. You are not the first Indian student anyone has seen.
- **Cebu itself.** Cheaper than Manila, safer than the reputation of big cities, and small enough that you learn it in a month.

*The trade*

## What you give up

- **No in-house FMGE coaching.** This is the big one. At Gullas or Perpetual the coaching comes to you. Here you buy an online course and hope you have the discipline. Many students do not.
- **Administration is slow.** Documents, transcripts and letters take longer than they should. Budget extra weeks for anything official, and never leave it to the last week before a deadline.
- **The campus can feel impersonal.** It is a large university, not a small college. You are one of many, especially in the first two years.
- **Indian food is only okay.** You will find it, but a decent Indian mess is not around the corner. Learn to cook.
- **Quiet social life if you do not make an effort.** Cebu is fun, but nothing is arranged for you. The first six months are lonely unless you join something.

*Fit*

## Who should pick it

A self-directed student who wants the hospital more than the classroom, who will buy an FMGE course without being told, and who does not need a large Indian crowd to feel at home. It also suits someone who wants a university name that carries some weight locally in Cebu.

*Not for*

## Who should skip it

Anyone who needs structured coaching built into the campus, anyone who struggles without a peer group from home, and anyone who gets defeated by paperwork. [Gullas](#gcm-gullas) solves the first, [Perpetual](#perpetual) the second.

*Money*

## What to ask the college for

**Fees and facilities:** this college does not publish a fee sheet or a facilities list online. Ask the admissions office for the current fee sheet, the affiliated teaching hospital, and the on-campus facilities list, in writing.

Fees change by intake, so no number is printed here. Write to the admissions office and ask for these in writing:

1. ### The current annual fee sheet

   With the academic year printed on it, and the total across the whole programme.
2. ### Hostel cost and what it includes

   Monthly or per semester, and how far it is from the hospital you will rotate in.
3. ### The refund policy in writing

   Especially if the visa is refused or you withdraw before enrolment.
4. ### The internship hospital and duration

   Which hospital, how long, and confirmation that it meets NMC's onsite requirement.
5. ### Which fees are payable in pesos on arrival

   Some charges are local and do not appear in the quotation you get in India.

Then add flights, visa renewal, insurance and living costs. The [cost page](/fees-and-cost/) walks through every line.

## Before you pay anyone

**Verify, in this order.**

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the college itself.

A Southwestern seat quoted at a price that does not match the college sheet is carrying something extra, and that something is not a college fee.

Official website: [swu.edu.ph](https://swu.edu.ph). For direct fee breakdowns and unbiased guidance, contact Dr. Nitz.

[The document checklist](/admission-process/#documents) for this intake.

*Las Piñas, Metro Manila*

## University of Perpetual Help System DALTA (UPHSD)

The largest Indian medical student community in the Philippines, located in Metro Manila. Features full in-house Indian messes, campus-based FMGE coaching, and direct training at the University of Perpetual Help DALTA Medical Center. Higher city living costs and urban congestion are the primary trade-offs.

*★★★★☆ Reviewed November 2026. Verified from official UPHSD documentation, CHED/NMC listings, and verified student feedback.*

## About the College

Founded in 1975 by Dr. Jose de Guzman Tamayo and Dr. Josefina Laperal Tamayo, the University of Perpetual Help System DALTA is a comprehensive university system anchored in medical and health sciences. The College of Medicine in Las Piñas is recognized by WHO (WDOMS) and NMC, maintaining one of the highest concentrations of foreign medical students in Southeast Asia.

> **Official Motto:** *"Character Building is Nation Building"* (Latin: *"In Omnia Paratus"*)  
> **Official Vision:** *"To emerge as a premier university delivering the total spectrum of healthcare and producing prime healthcare providers."*  
> **College Mission:** *"To develop physicians who are experts in human biology, properly endowed with values oriented to the optimum care of the patient."*

## The facts

Location & Address
:   Alabang-Zapote Road, Pamplona 3, Las Piñas City, Metro Manila, 1740 Philippines

Programme Structure
:   BS Biology + 4-Year Doctor of Medicine (MD) + 12-Month Clinical Internship (Total 5.5–6 Years; NMC 54+12 Month Compliant)

Instruction Language
:   English (100% of lectures, practicals, exams, and ward rounds)

FMGE / NExT Coaching
:   Yes, structured on-campus coaching by visiting Indian medical educators

Official Website
:   [perpetualdalta.edu.ph](https://perpetualdalta.edu.ph)

**The short version.**

The gentlest transition for students who require an established Indian peer support system, Indian dining facilities, and structured coaching on campus. The trade-offs are higher Metro Manila rent, daily traffic along Alabang-Zapote Road, and a crowded batch.

**Information sourcing.**

Compiled from official UPHSD medical school circulars, hospital bed occupancy filings, and current Indian student association records.

## International Student Facilities

- **International Students Help Desk:** Full-time International Student Affairs office dedicated to processing 9(F) student visa conversions, Bureau of Immigration filings, and annual NBI clearances.
- **Hostel Accommodation:** Comprehensive male and female student hostels located in Pamplona 3 and around campus with 24/7 biometric security and air conditioning.
- **In-House Indian Mess:** Multiple operating Indian messes serving authentic North and South Indian vegetarian and non-vegetarian meals daily.
- **Clinical Hospitals:** University of Perpetual Help DALTA Medical Center (500-bed tertiary university hospital right on campus), supplemented by government rotations at San Lazaro Hospital, Ospital ng Maynila, and Bacoor District Hospital.
- **Scholarships & Merit Concessions:** Academic honor incentives for top-ranking students maintaining dean's list distinction.

*The good*

## What works here

- **The Indian community is the biggest of the six.** Seniors who have cleared FMGE, notes passed down, someone to tell you which hostel is a trap on your first week. That network is worth more than it sounds.
- **FMGE coaching is established.** Not a token weekend session. The coaching here has a track record and it runs alongside the course.
- **Indian food is genuinely available.** Restaurants, grocery stores with spices, and mess options. If food is the thing that would break you, this is the college that removes it.
- **Hospital exposure is solid.** Metro Manila hospitals see a very wide case mix, and students get into the wards.
- **Easy to reach India.** More flights out of Manila than out of Cebu or Davao, which matters when there is an emergency at home.

*The trade*

## What you give up

- **Traffic and pollution.** A commute that should take twenty minutes takes an hour. That hour comes out of your study time, every day, for five years.
- **A higher cost of living.** Rent, food and transport all cost more than Cebu or Davao. Budget accordingly, not by the college's first-year quote.
- **Distraction.** A large Indian batch can be a comfort or a party, depending on the company you keep. Several students say they studied better after moving apartments away from the group.
- **You are one of many.** Large cohort, and the campus is a business. Do not expect to be chased if you fall behind.

*Fit*

## Who should pick it

A student who knows their limit and wants support built in: people from home, food from home, and coaching in the building. It also suits a family that values being able to reach the student with a short flight.

*Not for*

## Who should skip it

Anyone who needs quiet and cheap, and anyone who is easily pulled into a crowd. If you know you will spend more evenings out than in the library, a smaller batch in Cebu or Davao is a better fit. See [Southwestern](#southwestern) or [Brokenshire](#brokenshire).

*Money*

## What to ask the college for

**Fees and facilities:** this college does not publish a fee sheet or a facilities list online. Ask the admissions office for the current fee sheet, the affiliated teaching hospital, and the on-campus facilities list, in writing.

Manila changes the monthly arithmetic more than the college does. Ask for both:

1. ### The current fee sheet, with the year on it

   Annual tuition and the total across the programme, not a per-semester figure that hides the rest.
2. ### Hostel cost, and what a nearby apartment costs

   Ask students, not the office. The office will quote the hostel; the students will tell you what rent actually is.
3. ### Whether coaching is included or separate

   And what it costs in the years it runs.
4. ### The refund policy if the visa is refused

   In writing, before any transfer.
5. ### Which hospital you rotate in

   And how you get there. In Manila, distance is measured in time, not kilometres.

Compare the full five-year total, not the first year. The [cost page](/fees-and-cost/) shows how the city changes the number.

## Before you pay anyone

**Verify, in this order.**

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the admissions office.

Perpetual is one of the most recommended colleges in the country, because it is popular and easy to reach. Popular is not the same as right for you.

Official website: [perpetualdalta.edu.ph](https://perpetualdalta.edu.ph). For direct fee breakdowns and unbiased guidance, contact Dr. Nitz.

[The document checklist](/admission-process/#documents) for this intake.

*Davao City*

## Davao Medical School Foundation (DMSF)

The leading clinical hub in Mindanao, offering massive patient exposure at the 1,500-bed Southern Philippines Medical Center. Known for its advanced 3D virtual dissection anatomy simulation center and structured FMGE training in one of the safest cities in the Philippines.

*★★★★☆ Reviewed November 2026. Verified from official DMSF institutional reports, hospital rotation agreements, and current student feedback.*

## About the College

Established in 1976 as a consortium between Ateneo de Davao University, Brokenshire College, and the San Pedro Hospital, the Davao Medical School Foundation is the pioneer medical school in Davao. Recognized by WHO (WDOMS) and NMC, DMSF is widely cited for having the highest clinical patient volume among Philippine medical institutions through its affiliation with SPMC.

> **Institutional Vision:** *"Healthy communities enjoying a quality life."*  
> **Institutional Mission:** *"To provide humane, integral health sciences education and services with an emphasis on primary health care in instruction, research, and community engagement."*

## The facts

Location & Address
:   Medical School Drive, Bajada, Poblacion District, Davao City, 8000 Davao del Sur, Philippines

Programme Structure
:   BS Pre-Med + 4-Year Doctor of Medicine (MD) + 12-Month Clinical Internship (Total 5.5–6 Years; NMC 54+12 Month Compliant)

Instruction Language
:   English (100% of lectures, practicals, exams, and ward rounds)

FMGE / NExT Coaching
:   Yes, extensive face-to-face coaching by visiting Indian medical specialists

Official Website
:   [dmsf.edu.ph](https://dmsf.edu.ph)

**The short version.**

Unmatched clinical case variety and patient flow in Mindanao. Davao City is clean, strictly governed, and safe. Higher tuition and flight logistics (connecting through Manila/Cebu) are the primary trade-offs.

**Information sourcing.**

Compiled from DMSF official academic catalogs, Southern Philippines Medical Center clinical rotation logs, and active student council data.

## International Student Facilities

- **International Students Help Desk:** Active Foreign Students Liaison Office assisting with Bureau of Immigration compliance, ACR I-Cards, and local Davao police checks.
- **Hostel Accommodation:** Separate men's and women's student residences in Bajada with biometric door locks, study lounges, and security guards.
- **In-House Indian Mess:** On-site and hostel-affiliated Indian messes serving North and South Indian home-style food.
- **Clinical Hospitals:** Southern Philippines Medical Center (SPMC - government apex facility with 1,500+ beds and highest patient density in Mindanao), DMSF Hospital (100-bed campus facility), and Davao Doctors Hospital.
- **Advanced Facilities:** 3D Anatomage digital tables, clinical simulation mannequins, computerized bone labs, and modern pathology libraries.
- **Scholarships & Merit Concessions:** Foundation merit fee concessions awarded to top academic performers per term.

*The good*

## What works here

- **The anatomy lab is a real advantage.** The 3D table helps when a cadaver is not available. It is a teaching aid, not a substitute for dissection, but it makes first year easier to understand.
- **High patient inflow.** You see a wider variety of cases here than in smaller hospitals, and variety is what makes clinical years useful.
- **FMGE coaching by Indian doctors.** People who sat the exam themselves, teaching for it. Different from a generic campus course.
- **A functioning Indian mess.** Food is settled, which removes a first-year stressor that most students underestimate.
- **Davao is calmer and safer than its reputation.** Five and a half years in Cebu and several trips to Davao, with no trouble walking at night. It is a smaller, more orderly city than Manila.

*The trade*

## What you give up

- **The fee is higher than the Cebu colleges.** You are paying for the lab, the hospitals and the coaching. Decide whether those are worth the difference to you.
- **Distance.** A longer trip home, fewer direct flights, and an extra connection when there is an emergency. For some families that is the deciding factor.
- **It can feel isolating.** Smaller city, smaller Indian crowd than Manila, and less to do on a weekend. If you need a social scene, Davao will not provide it.
- **Being the best-funded student does not make it the best fit.** A few students arrive expecting the fee to solve motivation. It does not.

*Fit*

## Who should pick it

A student whose priority is clinical exposure, whose family can absorb the higher fee, and who is comfortable in a quieter city. It suits someone who wants coaching from people who have cleared the exam rather than a general prep course.

*Not for*

## Who should skip it

Anyone on a tight budget, anyone who needs a big Indian crowd, and anyone who will be flying home more than once a year. The cheaper Cebu options do the job. See [Gullas](#gcm-gullas) or [Southwestern](#southwestern).

*Money*

## Fees for the 2026-2027 intake

Published by the college for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges (enrolment, Level 1 semesters, documentation, visa, ticketing, books) are already quoted in rupees.

Fee sheet, Davao Medical School Foundation, 2026-2027

| Particular | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Enrolment fee | Rs 2,50,000 |
| Level 1, 1st semester | Rs 2,50,000 |
| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,50,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing and other services | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Book fee | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | USD 2,750 (Rs 2,54,871) |
| Food and accommodation per month | 15,000 PHP (Rs 21,716) |

- FMGE coaching: face-to-face coaching by Indian doctors, on the DMSF and KINGS campus.
- Visa costs in the Philippines: visa conversion and extension are paid by the student at actual cost.
- Refund: the enrolment fee is not refunded.
- Internship: the fee for the one-year internship is discussed at the time of internship.

**Campus facilities:** Hospital, hostel, cadaver lab, library, laboratory, 3D Anatomage, hostel rooms, mess hall.

**What the admissions package includes:** MEA and foreign-affairs authentication, apostille of academic documents, visa appointment and preparation, embassy visa interview fee, visa from the Philippines embassy in India, foreign-exchange assistance, one India-Philippines flight ticket, airport pickup and transfer to the hostel, and a Philippines mobile SIM.

*Fees change every intake. Confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay, and use the ask list below for the lines the sheet does not cover.*

*Money*

## What to ask the college for

The price difference between DMSF and Cebu is real, so get it itemised rather than quoted as one lump:

1. ### Tuition per year and the programme total

   With the academic year printed on the sheet.
2. ### What the anatomy lab access costs

   Included in tuition or charged separately. Ask directly.
3. ### Hostel and mess costs, separately

   Mess is often the line that changes between the quote and the reality.
4. ### Coaching fees and when they start

   Which year, how many hours, and whether attendance is required.
5. ### The refund policy in writing

   Particularly if the visa is refused.
6. ### The internship hospital and its NMC compliance

   Which hospital, how long, and confirmation of the onsite requirement.

Add the flights. Davao costs more to reach than Cebu, twice a year, for five years. [The full cost page](/fees-and-cost/) includes that line.

## Before you pay anyone

**Verify, in this order.**

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the admissions office.

DMSF is also frequently sold with a package that includes hostel and coaching. Ask for each part priced separately so you can see what you are actually buying.

Official website: [dmsf.edu.ph](https://dmsf.edu.ph). For direct fee breakdowns and unbiased guidance, contact Dr. Nitz.

[The document checklist](/admission-process/#documents) for this intake.

*Davao City*

## Brokenshire College School of Medicine

A low-distraction, small-batch medical school in Davao City with a high faculty-to-student ratio. Features personalized mentoring and clinical training at Brokenshire Memorial Hospital, suited for students who thrive in calm environments without overwhelming crowds.

*★★★☆☆ Reviewed November 2026. Verified from official Brokenshire academic bulletins, hospital records, and student reviews.*

## About the College

Founded in 1954 under the United Church of Christ in the Philippines (UCCP) and expanding to medicine in 2016, Brokenshire College operates on its scenic hilltop campus in Madapo. Recognized by WHO (WDOMS) and NMC, it emphasizes patient-centered, community-oriented medicine with intimate classroom cohorts.

> **Official Motto:** *"Fides et Servitium"* (Faith and Service)  
> **Official Vision:** *"A leading Christian learning institution enabling medical learners to make a difference in the world."*  
> **Mission Goal:** *"To develop multi-potential medical graduates equipped as clinicians, researchers, managers, and social health advocates."*

## The facts

Location & Address
:   Brokenshire Heights, Madapo, Barangay 8-A, Davao City, 8000 Davao del Sur, Philippines

Programme Structure
:   BS Biology + 4-Year Doctor of Medicine (MD) + 12-Month Clinical Internship (Total 5.5–6 Years; NMC 54+12 Month Compliant)

Instruction Language
:   English (100% of lectures, practicals, exams, and ward duties)

FMGE / NExT Coaching
:   Yes, on-campus structured preparation

Official Website
:   [brokenshire.edu.ph](https://brokenshire.edu.ph)

**The short version.**

Small batches where professors know every student by name. The environment is calm, supportive, and studious. Clinical volume at the attached hospital is moderate compared to government mega-centers like SPMC.

**Information sourcing.**

Compiled from Brokenshire College registrar notices, hospital department rosters, and verified graduate reports.

## International Student Facilities

- **International Students Help Desk:** Dedicated foreign student coordinator for student visa 9(F) processing, conversions, and local documentation.
- **Hostel Accommodation:** Quiet on-campus residential halls set in the green Madapo heights with 24/7 security personnel.
- **In-House Indian Mess:** On-campus Indian dining service with options for both vegetarian and non-vegetarian students.
- **Clinical Hospitals:** Brokenshire Memorial Hospital (300+ bed tertiary multi-specialty teaching hospital), plus supplemental rotations at SPMC and regional health centers.
- **Scholarships & Merit Concessions:** UCCP institutional scholarships and academic performance fee reductions for qualifying students.

*The good*

## What works here

- **Small batches.** Faculty learn your name and notice when you are slipping. In a batch of hundreds, nobody notices.
- **A cadaver lab.** Actual dissection, which several students at bigger colleges only get through a screen and a model.
- **Accessible professors.** You can ask a question after class and get an answer, not a form.
- **A quieter environment.** Davao is calmer, the campus is calmer, and there is less to spend money on. For a student who gets distracted, that is a feature.
- **FMGE coaching available.** Not the strongest of the six, but present.
- **Indian mess nearby.** You will not have to cook every day, which is more than JMC can offer.

*The trade*

## What you give up

- **The attached hospital is smaller.** This is the one to weigh hardest. Fewer patients means fewer cases, and clinical years are where case volume turns into judgement.
- **Fewer Indian students.** A small community is close, but it is also small. If your first year depends on having a group from home, this will be hard.
- **Davao is far from India.** Longer flights, fewer direct options, and an extra connection when something happens at home.
- **Little nightlife or city life.** If you need a city to enjoy, this is not it.
- **Less name recognition.** It is a legitimate college, but it is not a name that opens doors on its own. Nothing in the Philippines really does; your FMGE score does.

*Fit*

## Who should pick it

A student who learns best in a small room, wants dissection, and does not need a crowd or a city. It also suits a family that wants the college to notice their child.

*Not for*

## Who should skip it

Anyone who needs maximum clinical volume should look at [DMSF](#dmsf). Anyone who needs a large Indian community should look at [Perpetual](#perpetual). If budget is the constraint, see [Gullas](#gcm-gullas).

*Money*

## Fees for the 2026-2027 intake

Published by the college for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges (enrolment, Level 1 semesters, documentation, visa, ticketing, books) are already quoted in rupees.

| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing and other services | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Book fee | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | 1,10,000 PHP (Rs 1,59,250) |

- FMGE coaching: face-to-face coaching by Indian doctors, on the Brokenshire and KINGS campus.
- Visa costs in the Philippines: visa conversion and extension are paid by the student at actual cost.

*Fees change every intake. Confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay, and use the ask list below for the lines the sheet does not cover.*

*Money*

## What to ask the college for

The appeal here is value with attention, so make sure the quote covers both:

1. ### The current fee sheet

   Annual and total, with the academic year on the document.
2. ### Hostel and mess, priced separately

   And how far the hostel is from the hospital where you will rotate.
3. ### The batch size for your intake

   Ask for a number, not "small". Small is the entire reason to choose this college.
4. ### Which hospital you rotate in, and its bed count

   Bed count is a rough proxy for case volume. If the answer is vague, that is information too.
5. ### Refund policy in writing

   Before any transfer.
6. ### Internship confirmation for NMC

   Which hospital, how long, and that it meets the onsite requirement.

[The cost page](/fees-and-cost/) shows how this fits into a five-year total.

## Before you pay anyone

**Verify, in this order.**

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the admissions office.

Small colleges are sometimes described as "easier to get into". Admission is not the bottleneck. Registration in India is.

Official website: [brokenshire.edu.ph](https://brokenshire.edu.ph). For direct fee breakdowns and unbiased guidance, contact Dr. Nitz.

*Sasa, Davao City*

## Jose Maria College of Medicine (JMC)

The lowest tuition fee among the recognized medical institutions in the Philippines. Located in suburban Sasa, Davao City, with medical missions and community rotations. Best suited for cost-conscious students prepared to cook and live simply in a small Indian batch.

*★★★☆☆ Reviewed November 2026. Verified from official JMC documentation, CHED permits, and enrolled student reports.*

## About the College

Founded in 2000 and establishing its College of Medicine in 2019, JMC is located along the Philippine-Japan Friendship Highway near Davao International Airport. Recognized by CHED, WHO (WDOMS), and NMC, it operates with modern lecture classrooms and a population-oriented primary care focus.

> **Official Motto:** *"Assured, Consistent, and Quality Education (ACQ)"*  
> **Institutional Vision:** *"To become a world-class institution producing globally competitive, adaptive leaders and community-oriented physicians."*  
> **Mission Statement:** *"To provide excellence in medical instruction, research, and community extension meeting international healthcare standards."*

## The facts

Location & Address
:   Phil-Japan Friendship Highway, Catitipan, Sasa, Buhangin, Davao City, 8000 Philippines

Programme Structure
:   BS Biology + 4-Year Doctor of Medicine (MD) + 12-Month Clinical Internship (Total 5.5–6 Years; NMC 54+12 Month Compliant)

Instruction Language
:   English (100% of lectures, practicals, exams, and ward rounds)

FMGE / NExT Coaching
:   Yes, on-campus preparatory guidance

Official Website
:   [jmc.edu.ph](https://jmc.edu.ph)

**The short version.**

The lowest overall entry price and fee structure of the six colleges. However, the Indian community is tiny, amenities in Sasa are suburban, and students must be comfortable cooking their own meals.

**Information sourcing.**

Compiled from JMC official circulars, CHED accreditation records, and direct verified student accounts.

## International Student Facilities

- **International Students Help Desk:** International admissions office handling visa endorsements, quarantine clearances, and police verifications.
- **Hostel Accommodation:** Budget-friendly dormitories on campus with basic security and study desks.
- **Food & Living:** Very limited Indian mess presence; students rely heavily on induction stoves and self-cooking.
- **Clinical Hospitals:** Affiliated regional tertiary training hospitals across Davao including rotations at Southern Philippines Medical Center.
- **Scholarships & Merit Concessions:** ACQ Academic Honors tuition discounts awarded to high-scoring students each semester.

*The good*

## What works here

- **The lowest total cost of the six.** Not the lowest first-year quote. The lowest five-year total, which is the number that matters.
- **Medical missions.** Community health work in barangays, with real patients and limited equipment. It teaches you to examine and decide without a CT scan, which is a skill you will need in India.
- **Small community.** The Indian students who are here tend to be close, because there is no big batch to disappear into.
- **Basic but honest.** Nobody is selling you a luxury campus. What you see is what it is.
- **Often includes documentation help.** Some packages bundle the paperwork and visa guidance. Verify what is actually included, and check whether the price still works once you strip out the extras.

*The trade*

## What you give up

- **You will cook.** There is no Indian mess culture here. If you arrive unable to make dal and rice, your first month will be miserable and expensive.
- **A very small Indian community.** Fine if you make friends easily. Hard if you were counting on a crowd from home.
- **Basic infrastructure.** Smaller library, older equipment, fewer of the extras. Compare it honestly with Gullas before you decide the saving is worth it.
- **Fewer city amenities.** Sasa is not a student district. Weekends are quiet.
- **The lowest fee attracts its own risk.** Watch for brokers who add a "processing" charge on top of an already low fee. The saving evaporates in one payment.

*Fit*

## Who should pick it

A highly independent student with a hard budget ceiling, who can cook, who does not need company to function, and who wants community health experience. It suits someone who has already lived away from home.

*Not for*

## Who should skip it

First-time-away students, anyone who cannot cook, and anyone who needs a big Indian network. If the saving is the only reason you are considering it, check [Gullas](#gcm-gullas) first, because the difference may be smaller than you think once food and hostel are counted.

*Money*

## Fees for the 2026-2027 intake

Published by the college for the 2026-2027 intake. Exchange rate used: 1 PHP = Rs 1.4477 and 1 USD = Rs 92.6805, as of 22 November 2026. The Indian-side charges (enrolment, Level 1 semesters, documentation, visa, ticketing, books) are already quoted in rupees.

| --- | --- |

| Level 1, 1st semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Level 1, 2nd semester | Rs 2,25,000 |
| Documentation, visa, ticketing and other services | Rs 1,50,000 |
| Books and uniform fee | Rs 40,000 |
| MD tuition per semester | 1,20,000 PHP (Rs 1,73,727) |
| Food and accommodation per month | 15,000 PHP (Rs 21,716) |

- FMGE coaching: face-to-face coaching by Indian doctors, at JMCM and the KINGS campus in Chennai.
- Visa costs in the Philippines: visa conversion and extension are paid by the student at actual cost.
- Refund: the enrolment fee is not refunded.
- Internship: the fee for the one-year internship is discussed at the time of internship.

**What the admissions package includes:** MEA and foreign-affairs authentication, apostille of academic documents, visa appointment and preparation, embassy visa interview fee, visa from the Philippines embassy in India, foreign-exchange assistance, one India-Philippines flight ticket, airport pickup and transfer to the hostel, and a Philippines mobile SIM.

*Fees change every intake. Confirm the current sheet in writing before you pay, and use the ask list below for the lines the sheet does not cover.*

*Money*

## What to ask the college for

A low fee only saves you money if nothing gets added later:

1. ### The current fee sheet, with the year on it

   Annual and total across the programme.
2. ### Exactly what the package includes

   Documentation, visa assistance, hostel, mess. Priced separately, so you can see the value of each.
3. ### Hostel cost and kitchen access

   If you are cooking, confirm there is a kitchen and what it costs.
4. ### Any local charges payable in pesos

   These are usually the ones missing from the quote you get in India.
5. ### Refund policy in writing

   Before any transfer, especially for a college sold as a package.
6. ### The internship hospital and NMC compliance

   Which hospital, how long, and confirmation of the onsite requirement.

Run the total through the [cost page](/fees-and-cost/), including food you will now be buying and cooking yourself.

## Before you pay anyone

**Verify, in this order.**

1. The college on the [NMC list](https://www.nmc.org.in). 2. The college on [WDOMS](https://search.wdoms.org). 3. The fee sheet from the admissions office.

Low-cost colleges are the ones where a "processing fee" of one lakh appears at the last minute. Ask for the full cost in writing before you commit.

Official website: [jmc.edu.ph](https://jmc.edu.ph). For direct fee breakdowns and unbiased guidance, contact Dr. Nitz.

[The document checklist](/admission-process/#documents) for this intake.

*Do this yourself*

## How to check any college in two minutes

Before you trust this page or anyone else's, check the two lists that decide whether the degree is worth anything in India.

1. ### Open the NMC list

   [nmc.org.in](https://www.nmc.org.in), then the list of recognised foreign medical institutions. Search the college name. If it is absent, stop.
2. ### Open the world directory

   [search.wdoms.org](https://search.wdoms.org). NMC's 2026 notice relies on this directory for verification, so a college missing here is a risk even if a brochure says otherwise.
3. ### Then read the college's own fee sheet

   Not a forwarded PDF. The version from the admissions office, with the year printed on it.

**About the ratings.**

Five stars does not mean Harvard. It means that for an Indian student with a normal budget, we would have few reservations about sending a younger cousin there.

Three stars means the college is legitimate and NMC-listed, but there is a specific trade we would want you to accept with your eyes open: a small hospital, a smaller batch, or a city with very little Indian food.

No college gets five stars here for facilities. The best facility in the Philippines is still not a match for a good Indian government college. What you are buying here is a seat, English-medium teaching and clinical access.

## Before you shortlist

*Rank any shortlist on three things: NMC listing, total cost, and whether the hospital is big enough to put you in front of patients. Each college page says which of those is the weakest.*
